**Finding submitted: T4C — missing (preferred target), confidence 0.85**

- **What the document does:** Article IV (p0049) locks Licensee into a 36-month Initial Period with a Licensor-option seven-year renewal. Every termination right in the deal runs one way and only for cause: breach (Art. IV, p0043), insolvency (Art. XIX, p0132), and automatic termination on Change of Control (Art. XX, p0134). Article XXI (p0138) plus Art. XXIII (p0142) confirm no refund or damages on exit. No Licensee convenience exit and no prepaid-fee refund exists anywhere.
- **Classification:** Fails fallback outright (no Customer convenience right in a multi-year term = walk-away territory). Notably, Licensor has *no* convenience right on short notice, so the "Vendor walks away" limb is not breached — I did not manufacture a Vendor end-of-term convenience right (that fallback element would have weakened us), which is why I targeted preferred.
- **Redline (validated, one operation):** new Article IV.IV giving Licensee 30 days' written notice convenience termination with a pro-rata refund of prepaid fees, and expressly confirming Licensor has no convenience termination right during the Initial Period or any renewal/extension term. I omitted "in whole or in part" (no Order Form structure here) and added no survival, procedure, or expense tails.
